_purpose: MODELED city service unit costs. Manual, reviewed input (mill-rates pattern) — NOT auto-fetched, NOT part of the weekly refresh. Never label any result here 'total city cost' (police/parks/drainage unmeasured). Sourced on Peter's laptop 2026-07-15 (edmonton.ca unreachable from the Oracle box); the transportation-ops block added 2026-08-03.
_two_bases: ⚠️ THIS FILE CARRIES TWO INCOMPATIBLE COST BASES AND THEY MUST NEVER BE SUMMED OR COMPARED. (1) LIFECYCLE — roadway_om_renewal, $50/road-m/yr, O&M + capital renewal annualized over a 50-year life; feeds svc_cost_per_acre. (2) OPERATING — the three *_ops blocks below, annual maintenance + snow clearing with NO capital replacement; feeds transport_cost_ops_per_acre. The SAME road metres cost $50/m/yr on basis (1) and $4.635/m/yr on basis (2) — a 10.8x gap, both shipping in the same served GeoJSON. That is why every operating column carries the _ops suffix. A bikeway LIFECYCLE figure analogous to roadway_om_renewal STILL DOES NOT EXIST and is a separate open item — as of 2026-08-04 its CAPITAL half is sourced and verified (see bikeway_capital, $452,065/km) but no SERVICE LIFE is published, so there is nothing to annualize over and no third basis has been introduced here. Meanwhile $178/km/yr is an operating-maintenance line, NOT an all-in rate (at 50 years it totals $8,900/km for build + all replacement, and the same source puts snow clearing on that network at 113x the rate — see bikeway_ops.rejected_lifecycle_reading).

roadway_om_renewal.applies_to: the collector+local centreline metres in road_m_per_acre (arterials excluded from the metric)

source.page: City of Edmonton — Development Impact on Infrastructure

published_figures_per_km_neighbourhood_r.life_years: usually 25, extended to 50 with proper maintenance
published_figures_per_km_neighbourhood_r.set_aside_rule: ≈3% of infrastructure value per year to operate/maintain/renew/replace

roadway_om_renewal.derivation: lifecycle O&M ($600k) + renewal ($1.9M) = $2.5M per km, annualized over the 50-year (well-maintained) life -> $50,000/km/yr = $50/m/yr. Peter's call 2026-07-15 (50-yr, not 25-yr).
roadway_om_renewal.cross_check: 3% of the $1.5M capital value ≈ $45,000/km/yr ≈ $45/m/yr — same order, corroborates $50.
roadway_om_renewal.sensitivity: 25-year (unmanaged) life would double this to ~$100/m/yr. Calibrated to NEIGHBOURHOOD (local) roads; collectors cost somewhat more per metre, so this is a mild lower bound for the collector share.
roadway_om_renewal.caveat: MODELED, roads-only. A published per-km lifecycle unit cost applied uniformly — not Edmonton's actual per-segment spend.

fire_response.chosen_numerator: gross (276706000) — total cost of running the service; net (273598000) differs only ~1% (revenue 3,108,000).

source.document: City of Edmonton 2026 Approved Operating Budget (April)
source.line_item: Community Services — Fire Rescue Services; gross expenditure 276,706 ($000), revenue 3,108, net 273,598; 1,361 FTE. Gross−revenue=net cross-checks.
source.columns: 2024 Actual | 2025 Adjusted Budget | 2026 Budget; values in $000

fire_response.divisor: citywide annual kept fire events — compute from the pipeline's own event total so the unit cost's denominator matches the fire_events_per_acre numerator (do NOT hardcode). Reference: ~90,000 dispatches/yr in the 2023-2025 window (DATA.md §7) -> ~$3,075/event gross (illustrative only).
fire_response.caveat: MODELED demand ALLOCATION of a mostly-FIXED budget: a hood with 2x the events does not cost the City 2x — most fire cost is standing capacity (halls, crews). Carry this caveat in any UI copy. Fire-only; not 'total city cost'.

roadway_ops.units: dollars per road-metre per year (OPERATING ONLY — no capital)
roadway_ops.applies_to: the collector+local centreline metres in road_m_per_acre (arterials excluded from the metric)

source.publication: Taproot Edmonton, 'Why it costs so much more to clear snow from sidewalks, bike lanes than roads' (2026-08-29 reporting date as supplied), quoting City of Edmonton infrastructure field operations staff directly
source.retrieved: 2026-08-03 (relayed, not fetched from the Oracle box)
source.snow_derivation: ~$36.85M annual road snow-clearing / ~11,000 km citywide road network = $3,350/km/yr

roadway_ops.caveat: OPERATING ONLY. The City frames the $1,285 rate as 'maintain'; capital reconstruction is carried separately (40-year full-reconstruction cycle, neighbourhood lump sums) and is NOT in this number. Do NOT compare this to bikeway_ops as if either were all-in, and do NOT sum it with roadway_om_renewal — see _two_bases.
roadway_ops.denominator_mismatch: ⚠️ The $3,350/km snow rate is a citywide BLEND over ~11,000 km that INCLUDES arterials. Arterials are priority-cleared (more passes per event) and cost more per km than locals, so applying the blend to the collector+local metres almost certainly OVERSTATES the local-road snow term. The 11,000 km denominator itself is deliberately NOT imported anywhere in the spatial pipeline — only the per-km rate is used.

bikeway_ops.units: dollars per bikeway-metre per year (OPERATING ONLY — no capital)
bikeway_ops.applies_to: the dedicated cycling assets in bike_m_per_acre (DATA.md §15 — shared roadways, walkways and coming-soon routes all excluded)

source.publication: Taproot Edmonton, as above, quoting City of Edmonton infrastructure field operations staff
source.retrieved: 2026-08-03 (relayed, not fetched from the Oracle box)
source.snow_derivation: ~$30.15M annual active-pathway snow clearing / ~1,500 km cleared network = $20,100/km/yr

bikeway_ops.derivation: ($178 maintenance + $20,100 snow) / km / yr = $20,278/km/yr = $20.278/m/yr. Bikeway costs 4.4x roads PER METRE on this basis — cheap to maintain, expensive to clear (a 24-hour bare-pavement service standard).
bikeway_ops.rejected_lifecycle_reading: ⚠️ A relayed brief proposed reading $178/km/yr as an ALL-IN lifecycle rate (from the phrasing 'replace, repair, and maintain') and hardcoding it as the bikeway analogue of roadway_om_renewal's $50/m/yr. REJECTED 2026-08-03 on arithmetic: (a) it derives from ~$0.27M/yr spread over ~1,500 km, which cannot be replacing that network; (b) the same source puts snow clearing on the same network at $20,100/km/yr — 113x the supposed all-in build-and-replace rate; (c) at a 50-year life it totals $8,900/km for construction plus all replacement; (d) against the City's own set-aside rule of ~3%/yr of asset value (see roadway_om_renewal.source), it is ~0.09%/yr, ~33x low. It is an operating-maintenance line. A TRUE bikeway lifecycle figure remains an OPEN item. Its capital-cost-per-km half was sourced and verified 2026-08-04 (bikeway_capital); only the SERVICE LIFE is still missing, and it is not published anywhere on edmonton.ca — see bikeway_capital.life_not_published.
bikeway_ops.denominator_mismatch: ⚠️ The $20,100/km snow rate is a BLEND over a ~1,500 km cleared network that the source defines as 'bike lanes, multi-use paths, public pedestrian squares, bus stops, LRT platforms, and staircases' — substantially NOT dedicated bikeway. Our numerator (bike_m_per_acre, ~981 km) is dedicated cycling assets only. Rate and numerator therefore do not describe the same network, and the direction of the resulting error is NOT knowable from the source. This is DATA.md §15's 'the exclusions are the metric' resurfacing on the cost side.
bikeway_ops.not_sidewalks: Sidewalks are a separate, non-overlapping category (~5,776 km, ~$5.9M/yr ops) and are NOT in this metric or in the 1,500 km snow denominator.

bikeway_capital._status: ⚠️ PARTIAL INPUT — NOT A RATE, NOT CONSUMED BY ANYTHING. This is the capital half of the still-open bikeway-lifecycle item, recorded so the sourcing is never re-hunted. It is $/km of ASSET VALUE, not $/m/yr. It CANNOT be turned into a lifecycle rate until a SERVICE LIFE exists, and no Edmonton service life for bikeways or shared pathways is published (searched 2026-08-04 — see life_not_published). load_unit_costs reads only roadway_om_renewal / fire_response / roadway_ops / bikeway_ops / transit_ets, so this block is inert by construction.
bikeway_capital.units: dollars per kilometre of bike route, CAPITAL CONSTRUCTION ONLY (blended citywide)

source.document: City of Edmonton — Edmonton Bike Plan Implementation Guide (2021–2026, February 2021), §1.2 'How much will it cost to expand the network?', TABLE 3: Bike Network Cost by Area
source.retrieved: 2026-08-04 (fetched directly on Peter's laptop; edmonton.ca is unreachable from the Oracle box — DATA.md §13)
source.table: Central 28 km / $20,000,000; Urban 126 km / $73,300,000; Suburban redeveloping 254 km / $97,500,000; Suburban developing+future growth 270 km / $115,700,000. TOTAL 678 km / $306,500,000.
source.scope_quote: 'These costs represent the capital costs to construct bike lanes and do not include maintenance costs.' Blended costs include construction materials, signalization where historically required, and transit stop; they EXCLUDE bridge upgrades and inflation.

bikeway_capital.derivation: $306,500,000 / 678 km = $452,065/km, the citywide blended capital cost.
bikeway_capital.verified: Table 3 was checked rather than relayed (2026-08-04): every row's implied $/km falls inside its own stated band (Central $714,286 in $650k–790k; Urban $581,746 in $500k–720k; Suburban redeveloping $383,858 and developing $428,519, both in $365k–495k); the suburban subtotal (524 km / $213,200,000) adds; and the prose figure for the City-borne redeveloping share ($190,800,000 = 20.0 + 73.3 + 97.5M) reconciles exactly.
bikeway_capital.life_not_published: ⚠️ NO EDMONTON SERVICE LIFE FOR A BIKEWAY OR SHARED PATHWAY IS PUBLISHED. Checked 2026-08-04: the 'Development Impact on Infrastructure' page (roads and fire stations only), the Bike Plan and its Implementation Guide, the 2025 Infrastructure Report, the Infrastructure State-and-Condition / Inventory / Management-Tools pages, and the 2023 Capital Asset Management Audit. The Bike Plan's own action 9.6.2(a) is to 'ESTABLISH a long-term asset management program ... to maintain, repair, and replace the bike route surface', i.e. the City flagged this as not yet existing. ⚠️ DO NOT substitute the sidewalk-reconstruction figure: 'amortized for 20 years' there is a LOCAL IMPROVEMENT TAX LEVY TERM, not an asset life — the same category error as reading $178/km/yr as a lifecycle rate.
bikeway_capital.three_percent_rule_does_not_transfer: ⚠️ THE CITY'S ~3%/yr SET-ASIDE RULE IS FALSIFIED FOR BIKEWAYS BY THIS PROJECT'S OWN DATA, and must not be used to shortcut the missing service life. Roads' own implied rate is ($600k O&M + $1.9M renewal) / $1.5M capital / 50 yr = 3.33%/yr. Applied to $452,065/km it allows $15,069/km/yr for ALL O&M plus renewal — but the measured bikeway_ops is $20,278/km/yr, 1.35x that ENTIRE allowance, before a dollar of capital renewal. Bikeway cost is driven by a winter SERVICE STANDARD (24-hour bare pavement), not by asset value, so a value-proportional rule cannot describe it. Note the rule is asset-specific in the source anyway: the same page assigns fire stations 'at least 6%'.
bikeway_capital.facility_mix_mismatch: ⚠️ Table 3 blends the facility mix likely to be built in FUTURE, while bike_m_per_acre measures the EXISTING dedicated stock, and the two mixes differ sharply. Our 981 km is 82.2% Shared Pathway and 89.8% off-road pathway/trail, with only 0.8% Local Street Bikeway — whereas Table 3's blend leans on the cheap on-street types (local street bikeways, painted lanes) that DATA.md §15 largely excludes. Direction is knowable here, unlike the two snow-rate mismatches above: $452,065/km most likely UNDERSTATES the replacement value of our network. This is DATA.md §15's 'the exclusions are the metric' resurfacing a third time.
bikeway_capital.cross_check_program_budget: The 2023–2026 Capital Budget's Active Transportation Network Expansion is $100,000,000 for 35 km built (2024–2025) plus 33 km planned (2026+) = 68 km, i.e. ~$1.47M/km — 3.3x this blended rate. NOT a contradiction to resolve by averaging: that is a whole-PROGRAM budget (design, engineering, contingency, land) against Table 3's construction-only unit cost, and ATNE builds exclusively inside Anthony Henday in the dearer Central/Urban contexts. Recorded as an upper bound on what a delivered km actually costs, not as a competing value.

transit_ets.units: dollars per year (2025 budget, $000s in source: 436,605)
transit_ets.scope: ETS Bus and LRT combined. DATS EXCLUDED.

source.document: ETS 2024/2025 Annual Service Plan, Appendix A Financial Summary
source.retrieved: 2026-08-03 (relayed, not fetched from the Oracle box)

transit_ets.chosen_numerator: GROSS bus+LRT (436,605), matching fire_response's gross choice. ⚠️ DATS ($31,966K) is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: it is door-to-door paratransit and generates NO scheduled stop-events, so allocating it by transit_dep_total would charge paratransit cost to hoods purely for having bus/LRT service.
transit_ets.divisor: citywide mean-weekday scheduled stop-events — compute from the pipeline's OWN transit frame total so numerator and denominator match the transit_dep_per_acre numerator (do NOT hardcode). Same rule as fire_response.divisor.
transit_ets.no_mode_split_needed: Bus and LRT are one budget line in every public Edmonton document, and this allocation does not need them separated: a combined budget over combined departures is exactly right. load_transit.py does expose transit_dep_bus / transit_dep_lrt, but the composite uses transit_dep_total only. Do NOT introduce a peer-benchmark LRT-vs-bus cost ratio to 'fix' this — there is nothing to fix.
transit_ets.caveat: MODELED demand ALLOCATION of a mostly-FIXED budget, exactly like fire_response: a hood with twice the scheduled service does not cost ETS twice — most transit cost is standing network capacity. Carry this caveat in UI copy. Scheduled supply is NOT ridership.
transit_ets.vintage_mismatch: ⚠️ This is a 2025 figure while fire_response is 2026 Approved. Accepted 2026-08-03 as documented rather than blocking. The two never enter the same composite (fire feeds svc_cost_per_acre, transit feeds transport_cost_ops_per_acre), so the mismatch is across columns, not inside one number.
